doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Max Roach, Abbey Lincoln and Papa Jo Jones
summary: Roach's odd meters, directing Abbey Lincoln's band, and learning jazz history from Papa Jo Jones at the Village Gate.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: No. It was — everything, because you know each was a different experience. Okay now when I was with Max Roach, you know we performed and Max loved to do all these different times. So I understood 5/4 but 7/4 and 13 and all that, that’s a little bit difficult. The 5/4 was natural for me. But he was married to Abbey Lincoln so when he sent me on © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

the road to be Abbey Lincoln’s musical director, and that was another good experience. But one night we was in New York and he called me and said, “You know Papa Jo Jones had had an engagement at the Village Gate” and he needed a keyboard player, or a pianist. And Max said, “Would you go to that,” because you know him and Papa Jo were really tight. He said, “I want you to go down there and work with Papa Jo. So you know I’m young, I’m thinking oh shoot, you know, Papa Jones. But actually that was one of the best experiences I had. Papa Jo taught me so much about history, you know, because he went back further than Max. And then he used to tell me about how the drummers and the tap dancers, they considered the tap dancers drummers but they were doing it with their feet. And they would exchange fours and eights. So that was, so you never know how you’re going to learn things.
